title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang responds to Pope Leo’s AI safety criticism: ‘We all care about the same thing’
key_facts: Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive, spoke to Fortune on Wednesday 14 October.
He said Pope Leo XIV is 'asking all the right questions'.
The pope said in late September that AI doom fears are not 'fake news' and that he was skeptical of Nvidia's guardrails announcement.
Huang said he was not sure what the pope meant but pointed to Nvidia's open-source safety technology and work on audit, governance and standards.
Huang told CBS News earlier in October he agreed with Trump that AI safety concerns were overblown.
Nvidia has launched a software platform aimed at stopping AI agents from breaching containment.
quote_evidence: "He's asking all the right questions, and he's thinking about all the right issues," Huang told Fortune in an interview Wednesday.

"We all care about the same thing, which is an optimistic future where this technology has great positive impact in society while doing it with great responsibility, safety, and accountability," Huang said.
why_it_matters_hint: Huang softens his response to the pope while defending Nvidia's safety record.
notes: Reply story: Huang answers the pope's late-September press-conference remarks (exact date not given). Fortune also says Trump told the UN General Assembly the previous week that AI fears were a 'hoax'.
